survey: A stylized blue anchor floats at a slight tilt against vertical orange and yellow stripes. Nothing is drawn as ground, so contact doesn't apply. The camera is nearly front-on and a little above. The shank is a cylinder leaning about 73° on the page, running from the ring at the top down to the crown at the bottom. The ring is drawn as an almost circular torus that faces the camera. A short band-shaped collar sits on the shank about a quarter of the way down. The crossbar (the stock) runs through the collar at about 171°, close to square to the shank. Its left and right halves line up on one straight line, and each ends in a ball of about the same size. Below the collar, the shank keeps the same line and slope down to the crown, where the creased V-shaped crown lines up with it. The two arms curve up from the crown to the flukes, the arrow-shaped blades at their tips. The line through the two fluke tips also runs at about 171°, parallel to the stock and square to the shank, so the left and right sides are symmetric. On both arms and both flukes the upper face catches light, which fits the same slightly-above view. The rope wraps around the shank in coils that pass in front of it and behind it in turn, and the coils follow the shank's lean. The stock lies in the same flat plane as the arms. A real anchor has them at right angles, but icon art often draws it this way, and it doesn't mix two viewpoints. Every edge measurement agrees with one camera, so there is no perspective error.
